newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says facilities ready to export oil.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says facilities ready to export oil.

text.p: Iraq said on Tuesday its oil installations were ready to export oil as soon as an oil-for- food deal signed with United Nations was put into effect.

"The oil ministry is ready to market Iraqi crude oil immediately after the implementation of the oil memorandum of understanding signed with the U.N. starting from the field to the oil terminal," the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya quoted the Oil Minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed as telling the Iraqi National Assembley.

Iraq and the U.N. signed the agreement on May 20 allowing Baghdad limited oil sales worth $2 billion renewable every six months to raise money to buy urgent needs for the Iraqi population, suffering from stringent U.N. trade sanctions imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The pact was about to be implemented in Septemeber but was halted when Baghdad sent in August troops to northern Iraq to help one Kurdish faction to fight against another.

Three U.N. oil experts visited Iraq earlier this month to see if the country's oil facitities can handle oil exports defined by the agreement which are estimated between 700,000 to 800,000 barrels per day. They are supposed to report their findings to the U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
Rasheed said his ministry was ready to sign contracts with foreign countries and multinational companies to invest in the Iraqi oil sector.
Elf Aquitaine representative in Iraq Yves J. Serre told Reuters on Monday the French energy group has already submitted an offer to Iraq to purchase oil as soon as the oil pact materialised.
China said on Monday that it was holding talks with Iraq on the possibility of signing oil exploration contracts.
Jumhouriya said on Tuesday in a front page article that Russian firms were conducting talks with Iraq to conclude oil deals to explore new oilfields and build oil loading terminals.
